text:
incident_bot: Pager: spike in 5xxs and cross-region latency anomalies detected in steering layer. Affected regions: apac-north1 receiving >40% of traffic from eu-west2 despite latency delta. Error rate now 24% (baseline 1.8%). Alert ID: RBW-CR-3067.

sarah_oncall: paging in — I'm seeing the alert, grabbing topology + recent deploys. No deploys in last 2h from product.

mike_neteng: looked at routing decisions — the latency scorer returned negative weight for eu-west2 for some prefix groups, and steering picked apac-north1. Looks like a regression in the latency weight normalization.

sarah_oncall: any quick way to stop bleed to apac while we triage?

mike_neteng: yes, we can temporarily override steering policy for the customer-tier /global path to force eu-west2 preferred. Doing a manual weight set now.

mike_neteng: running:
```bash
routingctl set-policy-weight --policy global-latency --prefix "/v1/generate" --region eu-west2 --weight 95
routingctl set-policy-weight --policy global-latency --prefix "/v1/generate" --region apac-north1 --weight 5
```

mike_neteng: applied — please confirm metrics.

chandra_prod: checking customer impact dashboards — top 5 tenants had ~30% errors before override. After override error rate for those tenants dropped to ~3-4% within 90s. Latency for eu-west2 rose slightly but still within SLO.

sarah_oncall: good. Marking mitigation: TEMP_OVERRIDE_EU_PREF. Notifying support to hold outbound notices until we have full RCA.

julia_support: noted. I'll stand by and prepare a short blast for customers if this stays >5m. Who's writing the impact blurb?

chandra_prod: I'll draft a customer blurb: short, factual, no technical blame. Draft in #support-drafts in 10.

ops_pager: added incident to on-call board and opened incident runbook entry. Severity set to Sev2 due to multi-region customer impact.

mike_neteng: digging into scorer code — saw a bad interaction when latency samples from a probe set include stale zone RTTs; normalization could produce inverted weights when stddev spikes. Repro locally with synthetic trace.

devops_bwd: I've captured a packet-level trace and TLS session mapping for a handful of failed requests, sending link to S3: s3://rbw-incidents/3067890123/traces.tar.gz

sarah_oncall: team — immediate asks: 1) Mike, continue root cause on latency scorer; 2) Devops, preserve traces and config snapshot; 3) Chandra, start quantifying customers hit and ETA for support message; 4) Julia, standby for handoff in 30m.

mike_neteng: working on a small fix to guard normalization against extreme stddev. Quick patch available, will test in staging. If tests pass, propose rollback of the recent latency-weight optimizer deploy from yesterday.

chandra_prod: customer impact so far: ~12 enterprise tenants with increased errors, ~45k failed requests in last 18m (~0.4% total platform requests). Most common path: /v1/generate. Financial exposure estimated low but supports flagged for potential SLAs.

sarah_oncall: decision: keep the manual override in place until tomorrow morning or until a safe code rollback can be applied. Logging mitigation as manual steering override.

julia_support: I'll prepare the customer note: "We experienced a routing anomaly that briefly increased errors for some requests; we've applied a temporary routing override and are monitoring. No action required from customers." Will post to #support-drafts.

ops_pager: automated monitors re-evaluating traffic — current aggregated 5xx back to 1.9% and latency distributions look stable. Continuing 1h observation window.

mike_neteng: staging tests for the normalization guard passed. Two options: 1) patch and deploy the guard across steering layer (low-risk, targeted), 2) rollback yesterday's optimizer deploy (broader). I recommend patch first.

sarah_oncall: do the patch. Coordinate with devops for a canary and quick metrics check.

devops_bwd: deploying canary of normalization-guard to steering-canary pool now. Canary will route 3% of traffic and emit debug logs.

mike_neteng: canary looks clean for 12m. No inverted weights on synthetic replay. Metrics: no spike in errors. Requesting rollout.

sarah_oncall: rollout approved. Mike, please push to prod with standard rollback window.

mike_neteng: rollback window passed, rollout complete. Observability shows stable weights and no recurrence of the inverted weight condition. Removing manual override in 5m and trending.

chandra_prod: customer impact update: errors for flagged tenants are back to baseline. Preparing final incidence summary for postmortem.

ops_pager: Incident marked RESOLVED at 3067891323 (root cause mitigated, monitoring in observation). Handing over to next on-call for postmortem.

julia_support: taking handoff. I'll coordinate the postmortem doc, confirm S3 artifacts, and publish a customer note in 1h.

sarah_oncall: handoff summary (for postmortem): cause = steering latency scorer normalization bug on high-variance RTT samples -> inverted weights -> cross-region misroute to apac-north1. Mitigation = manual routing override -> deploy normalization guard -> full rollout. Impact = 12 tenants, ~45k failed requests, severity Sev2. Next steps = RCA writeup, test suite for latency scorer edgecases, and an alert to catch inverted-weight condition.

incident_bot: Incident RBW-CR-3067 resolved by manual override + normalization-guard deploy. Postmortem channel: #incidents-pm-3067890123.

sarah_oncall: :thumbsup: Good job team. Closing thread once postmortem doc is published.
